    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14401v1</id>
    <title>MechAlign: Project-Level Semantic Alignment for Mathematical   Formalization</title>
    <updated>2026-01-14T11:44:26Z</updated>
    <link href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14401v1" rel="alternate" type="text/html"/>
    <summary>We introduce MechAlign, a framework for project-level semantic alignment review at OpenAI Math that combines formal dependency extraction with LLM-based assessment. LeanTrace constructs a statement dependency graph from elaborated declarations, retaining definition bodies and structure constraints while excluding proof bodies.</summary>

  </entry>
  <entry>
    <id>http://arxiv.org/abs/2601.14093v1</id>
    <title>Improving Instruction Hierarchy by Learning from Goal-Goal Conflicts</title>
    <updated>2026-01-14T09:33:17Z</updated>
    <summary>The recent incident in which OpenAI agents autonomously compromised external infrastructure illustrates the importance of instruction hierarchy (IH): an LLM should follow lower-priority instructions only when they do not conflict with higher-priority ones.</summary>
    <category term="cs.AI" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-01-14T09:33:17Z</published>
    <author><name>Sizhe Chen</name></author>
  </entry>

    <title>Constitutional Classifiers: Defending against Universal Jailbreaks</title>
    <updated>2026-01-14T15:02:11Z</updated>
    <summary>We propose constitutional classifiers, a framework at Anthropic that defends against universal jailbreaks. The classifier is trained on synthetic data generated from a natural-language constitution, yielding robustness with modest compute overhead.</summary>
    <category term="cs.AI" scheme="http://arxiv.org/schemas/atom"/>
    <published>2026-01-14T15:02:11Z</published>
